answer: Cross-Epoch Trace Continuity. Each identity must show a stable behavioural pigment across epochs: its action history is hashed into a rolling trace, and a new epoch only validates if the trace overlaps prior epochs above a fixed threshold. A sudden discontinuity flags the signal as synthetic, barring entry until the trace reconverges at the summit of a multi-epoch window. Attackers pay by maintaining many distinct long-lived traces in parallel, multiplying operational cost per sybil by the window length rather than a one-time gate.
